english: I want to pay.
notes: QUIERO = present tense of 'querer' (I want). Always followed by infinitive verb. No subject pronoun needed in Spanish.

english: I want to rest.
notes: QUIERO = present tense 'I want'. DESCANSAR = infinitive 'to rest'. Basic structure: want + action.

english: Can I pay with a card?
notes: PUEDO = present tense 'I can' (ability). CON = with (preposition). Uses infinitive after can/puedo.

english: Can I park here?
notes: AQUÍ = here (location). Inverted word order in Spanish questions: ¿Puedo... = Can I...? No do/does needed.

english: I need to find a hotel.
notes: NECESITO = 'I need' (present). UN = masculine article 'a'. Infinitive follows directly. Very common travel pattern.

english: I need to change money.
notes: CAMBIAR = infinitive 'to change'. DINERO = money (masculine). Essential for border/airport situations.

english: I am going to look for food.
notes: VOY A = 'I'm going to' (near future). A = preposition required before infinitive. BUSCAR = to look for.

english: I am going to leave early.
notes: SALIR = to leave/depart (infinitive). TEMPRANO = early (adverb). VOY A constructs future plans.

english: I have to check the motorcycle.
notes: TENGO QUE = 'I have to' (obligation). LA = feminine article (moto is feminine). QUE = required connector word.

english: I have to buy water.
notes: AGUA = water (feminine, though starts with 'a'). TENGO QUE = obligation/duty structure.

english: I am staying in this hotel.
spanish: Me estoy quedando en este hotel.
notes: ME = reflexive pronoun (comes before verb). ESTOY = present of estar. QUEDANDO = gerund (staying). ESTE = this (masculine demonstrative).

english: I have a reservation here.
notes: TENGO = 'I have' (present of tener). UNA = feminine article 'a'. Simple possession structure.

english: I am a guest of the hotel.
notes: SOY = 'I am' (identity/permanent state). DEL = de + el (of the, contracted). Identity statement uses SER not ESTAR.

english: Because there is a hotel here.
notes: PORQUE = because (conjunction). HAY = 'there is/are' (impersonal, never conjugates). UN = masculine article.

english: Because I need to rest.
notes: PORQUE connects clauses. NECESITO = present tense. Reason phrases always use present, not future.

english: Because I have to leave early.
notes: PORQUE = because. TENGO QUE = obligation. Reason phrase explains WHY (answering 'por qué').

english: Where is the hotel?
notes: DÓNDE = where (question word). ESTÁ = present of estar (location). ESTÁ always used for location, not SER.

english: Where can I park?
notes: DÓNDE + PUEDO + infinitive = 'Where can I...?'. Open-ended location question.

english: Is there parking here?
notes: HAY = there is/are (never changes). ESTACIONAMIENTO = parking (masculine). Yes/no question format.

english: Can you help me?
notes: ME = indirect object pronoun (to/for me). PUEDE = formal 'can you'. Pronoun goes before verb.

english: I am looking for a mechanic.
notes: BUSCO = present tense 'I look for/am looking for'. No auxiliary verb needed. Direct object follows.

english: There is a problem with the motorcycle.
spanish: Hay un problema con la moto.
notes: HAY = there is. UN = masculine article. CON = with (preposition). LA = feminine article for moto.

english: There is a hole in my inner tube.
spanish: Hay un agujero en la cámara.
notes: HAY = there is. EN = in (preposition). LA CÁMARA = the inner tube (feminine). Problem statement structure.

english: My inner tube has a hole.
notes: TIENE = 'has' (present of tener). LA CÁMARA = subject (inner tube). Alternative way to express same problem.

english: I need you to fix the inner tube.
notes: NECESITO QUE = 'I need that' (triggers subjunctive). REPARE = subjunctive 'you repair'. LA = feminine object.

english: Can you fix the inner tube?
notes: PUEDE = formal 'can you' (present of poder). Infinitive follows directly. Simpler than subjunctive version.

english: I have a reservation.
notes: TENGO = 'I have'. UNA = feminine article. Simple possession statement for check-in.

english: I need a room for one night.
spanish: Necesito una habitación para una noche.
notes: PARA = for (preposition). UNA NOCHE = one night (feminine). Complex noun phrase after necesito.

english: How much does it cost per night?
notes: CUÁNTO = how much (question word). CUESTA = costs (present of costar). POR = per (preposition).

english: Where can I park the motorcycle?
notes: DÓNDE PUEDO = where can I. LA MOTO = direct object (the motorcycle, feminine). Specific location question.

english: I need gas.
notes: NECESITO = I need (present). GASOLINA = gasoline (feminine). Essential travel phrase.

english: Is there a mechanic near here?
notes: HAY = there is. CERCA DE = near (preposition + de). AQUÍ = here. Yes/no question about service location.

english: The motorcycle won't start.
notes: NO = negation (goes before verb in Spanish). ARRANCA = starts (present of arrancar). LA = feminine article.

english: Can you check it, please?
notes: REVISARLA = check + it (LA is feminine object pronoun attached to infinitive). PUEDE = can you (formal).

english: I'm looking for an ATM.
notes: BUSCO = I look for (present). UN CAJERO AUTOMÁTICO = an ATM (literally 'automatic cashier').

english: Can you speak more slowly, please?
notes: PUEDE HABLAR = can you speak. MÁS DESPACIO = more slowly (comparative). Essential comprehension aid.

english: It is expensive.
notes: ES = 'it is' (identity/characteristic, not location). CARO = expensive (masculine form). Subject pronoun omitted.

english: It is cheap.
notes: BARATO = cheap (masculine). Use ES for permanent qualities, ESTÁ for conditions/location.

english: It is here.
notes: ESTÁ = 'it is' (location/condition, not identity). AQUÍ = here. Never use ES for location.

english: It is far.
notes: LEJOS = far (location descriptor). ESTÁ shows temporary/changeable state or location.

english: It is near.
notes: CERCA = near. Common response to location questions. ESTÁ for proximity/location.

english: I need it.
notes: LO = direct object pronoun 'it' (masculine). Always comes BEFORE conjugated verb. Not at end like English.

english: I have it.
notes: LO = masculine object pronoun. Word order: LO before verb. Mirror of English structure.

english: I want it.
notes: LO QUIERO = I want it. Pronoun placement before verb is non-negotiable in Spanish.

english: My motorcycle is broken.
notes: ESTÁ = is (condition). ROTA = broken (feminine adjective matching feminine 'moto'). Adjectives agree with nouns.

english: The tire is flat.
notes: LA LLANTA = the tire (feminine). DESINFLADA = deflated (feminine form). ESTÁ for conditions.

english: The chain is loose.
notes: LA CADENA = the chain (feminine). FLOJA = loose (feminine). Maintenance problem description.

english: I need oil.
notes: ACEITE = oil (masculine). Simple need statement for maintenance.

english: Fill it up, please.
notes: LLÉNALO = fill it (imperative + masculine object pronoun -lo). Tú command form. Command adds pronouns directly.

english: Is there secure parking?
notes: HAY = there is. SEGURO = secure/safe (masculine). Critical for overnight motorcycle storage.

english: The road has many holes.
notes: TIENE = has (present of tener). MUCHOS = many (masculine plural). AGUJEROS = holes.

english: The rain is very strong.
notes: LA LLUVIA = the rain (feminine). ES = is (characteristic/permanent). MUY = very (adverb intensifier).

english: I'm going to wait here.
notes: VOY A ESPERAR = I'm going to wait (near future). AQUÍ = here. Safety decision phrase.

english: Can you show me on the map?
notes: PUEDES = can you (tú form). MOSTRARME = show + me (infinitive with pronoun). EN EL MAPA = on the map.

english: Do you know a good mechanic?
notes: CONOCES = do you know (tú form of conocer, personal knowledge). BUEN = good (shortened before masculine noun).

english: The sun is very hot.
notes: ESTÁ CALIENTE = is hot (condition, changeable). CALIENTE = hot (temporary state). MUY = intensifier.

english: I want to take a photo.
notes: QUIERO TOMAR = I want to take. TOMAR = to take/make (photo). FOTO = photo (feminine).

english: Where can I wash my clothes?
notes: LAVAR = to wash (infinitive). MI ROPA = my clothes (feminine). Laundry/hygiene phrase.

english: The border crossing opens at six.
spanish: La frontera abre a las seis.
notes: ABRE = opens (present of abrir). A LAS SEIS = at six (time expression). LA FRONTERA = the border (feminine).

english: I need my passport.
notes: MI PASAPORTE = my passport (masculine). Critical document statement.

english: Can I leave my backpack here?
notes: DEJAR = to leave/deposit (infinitive). MI MOCHILA = my backpack (feminine). Storage request.

english: The tire pressure is too low.
spanish: La presión de la llanta está muy baja.
notes: LA PRESIÓN DE LA LLANTA = tire pressure (feminine). ESTÁ BAJA = is low (condition). DEMASIADO/MUY = too.

english: I'm looking for a place to camp.
spanish: Estoy buscando un lugar para acampar.
notes: ESTOY BUSCANDO = I'm looking (present progressive). PARA ACAMPAR = to camp. UN LUGAR = a place.

english: The wind is very strong.
notes: EL VIENTO = the wind (masculine). FUERTE = strong (changeable condition). ESTÁ not ES for weather conditions.

english: I want to send a package.
notes: QUIERO ENVIAR = I want to send. ENVIAR = to send/mail. UN PAQUETE = a package (masculine).

english: How many hours to the next city?
notes: CUÁNTAS HORAS = how many hours. HASTA = until/to (preposition). LA PRÓXIMA CIUDAD = next city (feminine).

english: The helmet is required by law.
spanish: El casco es requerido por ley.
notes: REQUERIDO = required (passive voice). POR LEY = by law (preposition phrase). Legal requirement statement.

english: I forgot my jacket.
notes: OLVIDÉ = I forgot (preterite, past action completed). MI CHAQUETA = my jacket (feminine).

english: Can you recommend a safe route?
notes: PUEDES RECOMENDAR = can you recommend (tú form). UNA RUTA SEGURA = a safe route (feminine).

english: I need to charge my phone.
notes: CARGAR = to charge (infinitive). MI TELÉFONO = my phone (masculine).

english: Is there WiFi in the hotel?
notes: HAY = there is. EN EL HOTEL = in the hotel (preposition + article + noun). Yes/no question.

english: The mountain pass is closed.
spanish: El paso de montaña está cerrado.
notes: EL PASO DE MONTAÑA = the mountain pass (masculine). ESTÁ CERRADO = is closed (condition/state).

english: I want to try the local food.
notes: PROBAR = to try/taste (infinitive). LA COMIDA LOCAL = the local food (feminine). Cultural experience phrase.

english: The police stopped me.
notes: ME DETUVO = stopped me (preterite). LA POLICÍA = the police (feminine, singular subject). Past action.

english: I need to see a dentist.
notes: VER = to see (infinitive). UN DENTISTA = a dentist (masculine). Medical emergency phrase.

english: The ferry leaves at noon.
notes: SALE = leaves/departs (present of salir). AL MEDIODÍA = at noon (preposition + article + noun).

english: The oil needs to be changed.
notes: NECESITA CAMBIARSE = needs to change itself (reflexive). Passive construction. CAMBIARSE = to be changed.

english: I'm going to follow this river.
notes: VOY A SEGUIR = I'm going to follow. ESTE = this (masculine demonstrative). RÍO = river (masculine).

english: The market is open only in the morning.
spanish: El mercado está abierto solo en la mañana.
notes: ESTÁ ABIERTO = is open (condition, masculine). SOLO = only (adverb). EN LA MAÑANA = in the morning.

english: I want to learn some local words.
notes: APRENDER = to learn (infinitive). ALGUNAS PALABRAS = some words (feminine plural). LOCALES = local.

english: The campsite has bathrooms.
notes: TIENE = has (present of tener). BAÑOS = bathrooms (masculine plural). Facility description.

english: I lost my wallet.
notes: PERDÍ = I lost (preterite, past completed action). MI CARTERA = my wallet (feminine).

english: Can you help me push the motorcycle?
notes: PUEDES AYUDARME = can you help me (indirect object ME). A EMPUJAR = to push (preposition A required).

english: The sunset from here is incredible.
spanish: La puesta de sol desde aquí es increíble.
notes: LA PUESTA DE SOL = the sunset (feminine). DESDE AQUÍ = from here. INCREÍBLE = incredible.

english: I need a tool to fix this.
notes: PARA ARREGLARLO = to fix it (infinitive + LO). PURPOSE phrase. UNA HERRAMIENTA = a tool (feminine).

english: The hostel is cheaper.
notes: MÁS BARATO = cheaper (comparative using MÁS + adjective). ES not ESTÁ for comparison. Price comparison.

english: I'm going to rest for two days.
spanish: Voy a descansar por dos días.
notes: VOY A DESCANSAR = I'm going to rest. POR DOS DÍAS = for two days (time duration). Rest stop planning.

english: The altitude is making me sick.
spanish: La altitud me está haciendo enfermo.
notes: ME ESTÁ HACIENDO = is making me (progressive + indirect object). ENFERMO = sick (masculine). Health problem.

english: Where can I get motorcycle insurance?
spanish: ¿Dónde puedo conseguir seguro para la moto?
notes: CONSEGUIR = to get/obtain (infinitive). SEGURO = insurance (masculine). PARA LA MOTO = for the motorcycle.

english: The road is unpaved.
notes: ESTÁ SIN PAVIMENTAR = is without pavement (negation + past participle). Condition/state description.

english: I want to meet other travelers.
notes: CONOCER = to meet/know (infinitive, personal knowledge). OTROS VIAJEROS = other travelers (masculine plural).

english: The customs officer wants to see my documents.
spanish: El oficial de aduana quiere ver mis documentos.
notes: QUIERE VER = wants to see (present of querer + infinitive). MIS DOCUMENTOS = my documents (masculine plural).

english: I'm going to avoid the highway.
notes: EVITAR = to avoid (infinitive). LA AUTOPISTA = the highway (feminine). Safety/route planning.

english: The tent is wet from the rain.
spanish: La carpa está mojada de la lluvia.
notes: LA CARPA = the tent (feminine). MOJADA = wet (feminine adjective). DE LA LLUVIA = from the rain (causation).

english: Can I pay in installments?
notes: EN CUOTAS = in installments/monthly payments. PAGAR = to pay (infinitive). Payment option question.

english: I need a veterinarian for my dog.
spanish: Necesito un veterinario para mi perro.
notes: UN VETERINARIO = a veterinarian (masculine). MI PERRO = my dog (masculine). Pet emergency.

english: The view from this mountain is worth it.
spanish: La vista desde esta montaña vale la pena.
notes: VALE LA PENA = is worth it (idiom, literally 'is worth the effort'). DESDE ESTA MONTAÑA = from this mountain.

english: I need to find a mechanic because the motorcycle will not start.
spanish: Necesito encontrar un mecánico porque la moto no arranca.
notes: NECESITO ENCONTRAR = I need to find. PORQUE = because. ARRANCA = starts. Linking reminder: PORQUE introduces the reason.

english: I want to check the chain before leaving.
spanish: Quiero revisar la cadena antes de salir.
notes: QUIERO REVISAR = I want to check. ANTES DE = before. Linking reminder: use ANTES DE + infinitive for the earlier action.

english: Can you repair the tire, or do I need a new one?
spanish: ¿Puede reparar la llanta o necesito una nueva?
notes: PUEDE REPARAR = can you repair. O = or. Linking reminder: O connects alternatives.

english: I am going to buy oil and also check the tire pressure.
spanish: Voy a comprar aceite y también voy a revisar la presión de las llantas.
pattern: voy a + infinitive; y también + clause
notes: Y TAMBIÉN = and also. Linking reminder: use Y TAMBIÉN to add another related action.

english: I am waiting for the mechanic, but I can leave later.
spanish: Estoy esperando al mecánico, pero puedo salir más tarde.
notes: PERO = but. Linking reminder: PERO introduces a contrast. MÁS TARDE = later.

english: The motorcycle is making a strange noise, so I am going to stop.
spanish: La moto hace un ruido extraño, entonces voy a parar.
notes: ENTONCES = so/then. Linking reminder: ENTONCES introduces the result or next action.

english: If the road is open, I can continue.
spanish: Si el camino está abierto, puedo continuar.
notes: SI = if. Linking reminder: SI introduces a condition. PUEDO CONTINUAR = I can continue.

english: Although it is raining, I am going to ride carefully.
spanish: Aunque está lloviendo, voy a conducir con cuidado.
notes: AUNQUE = although/even though. Linking reminder: AUNQUE introduces an obstacle or contrast.

english: After filling the tank, I am going to continue south.
spanish: Después de llenar el tanque, voy a continuar hacia el sur.
pattern: después de + infinitive; voy a + infinitive
notes: DESPUÉS DE = after. Linking reminder: use DESPUÉS DE + infinitive to sequence actions.

english: I need gasoline, and I also need water.
spanish: Necesito gasolina y también necesito agua.
notes: Y TAMBIÉN = and also. Linking reminder: it adds a second need.

english: I need a room for two nights and secure parking.
spanish: Necesito una habitación para dos noches y estacionamiento seguro.
notes: Y = and. Linking reminder: Y joins two related needs.

english: I want to see the room before paying.
spanish: Quiero ver la habitación antes de pagar.
notes: ANTES DE = before. Linking reminder: the verb after ANTES DE remains an infinitive.

english: Can I park the motorcycle here, or is there another place?
spanish: ¿Puedo estacionar la moto aquí o hay otro lugar?
notes: O = or. Linking reminder: O presents another option.

english: The room is clean, but it is too expensive.
spanish: La habitación está limpia, pero es muy cara.
notes: PERO = but. Linking reminder: PERO contrasts two descriptions.

english: I am tired, so I am going to stay here tonight.
spanish: Estoy cansado, entonces voy a quedarme aquí esta noche.
notes: ENTONCES = so/then. Linking reminder: the first idea causes the next decision.

english: If breakfast is included, I want the room.
spanish: Si el desayuno está incluido, quiero la habitación.
notes: SI = if. Linking reminder: SI states the condition for your decision.

english: After checking in, I am going to take a shower.
spanish: Después de registrarme, voy a ducharme.
pattern: después de + infinitive; voy a + infinitive
notes: DESPUÉS DE = after. REGISTRARME = to check in. Linking reminder: sequence the next action with DESPUÉS DE.

english: Although the hotel is simple, it is safe.
spanish: Aunque el hotel es sencillo, es seguro.
notes: AUNQUE = although. Linking reminder: AUNQUE acknowledges a contrast without changing the main point.

english: I want chicken with rice because I am very hungry.
spanish: Quiero pollo con arroz porque tengo mucha hambre.
notes: PORQUE = because. TENGO HAMBRE = I am hungry. Linking reminder: PORQUE explains the reason.

english: I can eat vegetables, but I cannot eat beef.
spanish: Puedo comer verduras, pero no puedo comer carne de res.
notes: PERO = but. Linking reminder: contrast what you can and cannot eat.

english: I am going to order breakfast and also a coffee.
spanish: Voy a pedir el desayuno y también un café.
pattern: voy a + infinitive; y también + addition
notes: Y TAMBIÉN = and also. Linking reminder: add another item with Y TAMBIÉN.

english: After eating, I need to pay.
notes: DESPUÉS DE = after. Linking reminder: use DESPUÉS DE + infinitive to show order.

english: Can I have water without ice and coffee without sugar?
spanish: ¿Puedo tomar agua sin hielo y café sin azúcar?
notes: Y = and. SIN = without. Linking reminder: Y joins two requests.

english: If the food is spicy, I need more water.
spanish: Si la comida es picante, necesito más agua.
notes: SI = if. Linking reminder: SI introduces the condition.

english: Although I am full, I want to try the dessert.
spanish: Aunque estoy lleno, quiero probar el postre.
notes: AUNQUE = although/even though. Linking reminder: AUNQUE connects two contrasting facts.

english: I am eating now, so I will pay later.
spanish: Estoy comiendo ahora, entonces voy a pagar más tarde.
notes: ENTONCES = so/then. MÁS TARDE = later. Linking reminder: ENTONCES introduces what follows.

english: I need to find the road to the next town.
spanish: Necesito encontrar el camino al próximo pueblo.
notes: NECESITO ENCONTRAR = I need to find. AL = a + el. Practical navigation structure.

english: Can I reach the city by this road?
spanish: ¿Puedo llegar a la ciudad por este camino?
notes: PUEDO LLEGAR = can I reach. POR ESTE CAMINO = by this road.

english: I am going to cross the bridge and then turn right.
spanish: Voy a cruzar el puente y después voy a girar a la derecha.
pattern: voy a + infinitive; y después + clause
notes: Y DESPUÉS = and then. Linking reminder: use it to give directions in sequence.

english: The gas station is close, but it is on the other side of the road.
spanish: La gasolinera está cerca, pero está al otro lado del camino.
notes: PERO = but. Linking reminder: add an important contrasting detail with PERO.

english: If I turn left here, will I reach the highway?
spanish: Si giro a la izquierda aquí, ¿llego a la carretera?
notes: SI = if. Linking reminder: use SI to test a possible route.

english: I need to arrive before dark because the road is difficult.
spanish: Necesito llegar antes de que oscurezca porque el camino es difícil.
pattern: antes de que + clause; porque + reason
notes: ANTES DE QUE = before. PORQUE = because. Two linking reminders: deadline first, reason second.

english: Although the map says left, the sign says right.
spanish: Aunque el mapa dice izquierda, el letrero dice derecha.
notes: AUNQUE = although. Linking reminder: use AUNQUE when two sources conflict.

english: I am lost, so I need help with the directions.
spanish: Estoy perdido, entonces necesito ayuda con las direcciones.
notes: ENTONCES = so/then. Linking reminder: state the problem, then its result.

english: I am learning Spanish because I am going to travel through Latin America.
spanish: Estoy aprendiendo español porque voy a viajar por Latinoamérica.
notes: PORQUE = because. Linking reminder: PORQUE explains your motivation.

english: I can speak a little, but I understand more.
spanish: Puedo hablar un poco, pero entiendo más.
notes: PERO = but. Linking reminder: contrast speaking ability with comprehension.

english: If you speak slowly, I can understand you.
notes: SI = if. HABLA is formal you. Linking reminder: SI introduces the helpful condition.

english: I want to practice, and I also want to learn local words.
spanish: Quiero practicar y también quiero aprender palabras locales.
notes: Y TAMBIÉN = and also. Linking reminder: add a second goal.

english: When I do not understand, I ask people to repeat.
spanish: Cuando no entiendo, pido que repitan.
notes: CUANDO = when. Linking reminder: CUANDO connects a recurring situation with your response.

english: I need help because I had an accident.
spanish: Necesito ayuda porque tuve un accidente.
notes: PORQUE = because. TUVE = I had. Linking reminder: PORQUE explains the emergency.

english: Can you call a doctor and also the police?
spanish: ¿Puede llamar a un médico y también a la policía?
notes: Y TAMBIÉN = and also. Linking reminder: add the second person or service needed.

english: I am hurt, so I need to go to the hospital.
spanish: Estoy herido, entonces necesito ir al hospital.
notes: ENTONCES = so/then. Linking reminder: connect the injury to the necessary action.

english: Although I can walk, my leg hurts a lot.
spanish: Aunque puedo caminar, me duele mucho la pierna.
notes: AUNQUE = although/even though. Linking reminder: contrast ability with pain.

english: If I feel worse, I am going to the clinic.
spanish: Si me siento peor, voy a ir a la clínica.
notes: SI = if. Linking reminder: introduce a possible condition and planned response.

english: I need medicine, but I do not know the name.
spanish: Necesito medicina, pero no sé el nombre.
notes: PERO = but. Linking reminder: state the need, then the problem.

english: Before taking this medicine, I want to speak with a doctor.
spanish: Antes de tomar esta medicina, quiero hablar con un médico.
notes: ANTES DE = before. Linking reminder: the first action must happen before the second.

english: I am going to call my family after I arrive at the hotel.
spanish: Voy a llamar a mi familia después de llegar al hotel.
pattern: voy a + infinitive; después de + infinitive
notes: DESPUÉS DE = after. Linking reminder: use DESPUÉS DE + infinitive for a later action.

english: I want to meet local people because I want to practice Spanish.
spanish: Quiero conocer gente local porque quiero practicar español.
notes: PORQUE = because. Linking reminder: explain your motivation with PORQUE.

english: I am traveling with my wife, and we both ride motorcycles.
spanish: Estoy viajando con mi esposa y los dos viajamos en moto.
notes: Y = and. LOS DOS = both of us. Linking reminder: Y adds a related fact.

english: When I have time, I like to talk with local people.
spanish: Cuando tengo tiempo, me gusta hablar con la gente local.
notes: CUANDO = when. Linking reminder: CUANDO connects an activity to the time it happens.

english: I'll check my documents while you look at the motorcycle.
spanish: Voy a revisar mis documentos mientras tú miras la moto.
notes: MIENTRAS = while. KEY: MIENTRAS shows two simultaneous actions. TÚ = you (informal).

english: I need to rest because the altitude is affecting me.
spanish: Necesito descansar porque la altitud me está afectando.
notes: PORQUE = because. KEY: PORQUE explains the reason. Use present tense for reason.

english: The hotel is more expensive than the hostel.
spanish: El hotel es más caro que el hostal.
notes: MÁS CARO QUE = more expensive than. KEY: MÁS + adjective + QUE forms comparatives. Use ES for permanent qualities.

english: I cannot leave until I find a mechanic.
spanish: No puedo salir hasta que encuentre un mecánico.
pattern: no puedo + infinitive; hasta que + subjunctive
notes: HASTA QUE = until. ENCUENTRE = subjunctive 'I find'. KEY: HASTA QUE signals a time limit or boundary condition.

english: The customs officer told me to open my backpack.
spanish: El oficial de aduana me dijo que abriera la mochila.
notes: DIJO = told (past). QUE + subjunctive follows indirect commands. ABRIERA = subjunctive 'open'.

english: I prefer to travel during the day.
notes: PREFIERO = I prefer (present of preferir). DURANTE = during (preposition). Route-planning statement.

english: As long as there is gasoline, I can go on.
notes: HAYA = subjunctive 'there is'. KEY: MIENTRAS + subjunctive for a condition to keep acting.

english: I'm tired from riding, but I want to reach the next town.
spanish: Estoy cansado de conducir, pero quiero llegar al próximo pueblo.
pattern: estar + adjective + de + gerund; pero + quiero
notes: CANSADO DE CONDUCIR = tired from riding. AL PRÓXIMO = to the next (al + el próximo). Fatigue + determination.

english: I'll come back when the road is safer.
spanish: Voy a volver cuando la carretera esté más segura.
notes: CUANDO = when. ESTÉ = subjunctive 'is' (future condition). KEY: CUANDO + subjunctive for future time.

english: Do you know whether the border is open?
notes: SI (conjunct.) = whether. SABES = do you know (tú form of saber). Practical yes/no information request.

english: The mechanic said the motorcycle will be ready tomorrow.
spanish: El mecánico dijo que la moto estará lista mañana.
notes: ESTARÁ = will be (future of estar). LISTA = ready (feminine). Timeline confirmation.

english: I would like to camp here if it is allowed.
spanish: Me gustaría acampar aquí si es permitido.
notes: ME GUSTARÍA = I would like (polite conditional). PERMITIDO = allowed (past participle as adjective).

english: The roads here are better than in the mountains.
spanish: Los caminos aquí son mejores que en las montañas.
notes: MEJORES = better (irregular form, not 'más buenos'). QUE = than. AQUÍ/EN = location contrast.

english: I'll stay here unless the weather gets worse.
spanish: Me quedaré aquí a menos que empeore el tiempo.
pattern: me quedaré + infinitive; a menos que + subjunctive
notes: A MENOS QUE = unless. EMPEORE = subjunctive 'gets worse'. KEY: Negation with condition.

english: I've been riding for six hours straight.
spanish: He estado conduciendo durante seis horas sin parar.
notes: HE ESTADO = I have been (present perfect). SIN PARAR = without stopping. Duration expression.

english: Whatever happens, I want to reach the coast.
spanish: Pase lo que pase, quiero llegar a la costa.
notes: PASE LO QUE PASE = whatever happens (fixed expression). COSTA = coast. Determination statement.

english: The longer we wait, the more expensive the fuel will become.
spanish: Cuanto más esperemos, más cara se volverá la gasolina.
notes: CUANTO MÁS...MÁS = the more...the more (proportional comparison). GASOLINA CARA = expensive gasoline.
